---
title: "Lab 02 — Simulation and Monte Carlo"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("lab_submission.R")
len <- read.csv("data/rivers.csv")$length_miles
mu <- mean(len); sigma <- sqrt(mean((len - mu)^2))
birthday_exact <- function(n) 1 - prod((365 - 0:(n - 1)) / 365)
set.seed(2027)
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab02", title = "Simulation and Monte Carlo", open = c("q9", "q10"))
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1  = "A Monte Carlo estimate of a probability p = 0.25 uses N = 10000 repetitions. Its standard error is about...",
  q2  = "What is the smallest group size n for which the probability of a shared birthday exceeds 0.9?",
  q3  = "In the Monty Hall game, a contestant who always switches wins with probability...",
  q4  = "In the dice game (A wins if the larger of the two dice is 4 or less), P(A wins) is...",
  q5  = "To simulate an exponential variable with rate 2 from U ~ Unif(0, 1) by the inverse transform, use...",
  q6  = "The running mean of rexp(n, rate = 2) converges, as n grows, to...",
  q7  = "Samples of size n = 30 are taken from the river lengths (sigma = 492 miles). The standard deviation of the sample mean is about...",
  q8  = "The normal approximation for P(sample mean > 700) with n = 30 gives about...",
  q9  = "The river lengths are strongly right-skewed. Why do the histograms of the sample means look normal for n = 30 or n = 100? How does the spread change when n is multiplied by 4?",
  q10 = "You want a Monte Carlo estimate ten times more accurate. How many more repetitions do you need, and why?"
)
```

## What you will do

Check the numbers from the lab, then answer the questions. `len` holds the 141 river lengths, with mean `mu` and standard deviation `sigma`; `birthday_exact()` is the function from the lab. Finish by downloading the `.txt` file.

## Monte Carlo estimates

```{r mc-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=8}
N <- 10000
p <- 0.25
sqrt(p * (1 - p) / N)                    # standard error of a Monte Carlo estimate
ns <- 1:80
which(sapply(ns, birthday_exact) > 0.9)[1]
(4/6)^2                                  # P(A wins) in the dice game
mean(pmax(sample(1:6, 1e6, TRUE), sample(1:6, 1e6, TRUE)) <= 4)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("0.0043", correct = TRUE),
  answer("0.043"),
  answer("0.25"),
  answer("0.0001"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## Distributions and the law of large numbers

```{r inv-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=6}
u <- runif(5000)
y <- -log(1 - u) / 2                     # inverse transform for Exp(2)
c(mean(y), 1/2, var(y), 1/4)
ks.test(y, "pexp", 2)$p.value
```

```{r q5}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q5"]],
  answer("-log(1 - U) / 2", correct = TRUE),
  answer("-2 * log(1 - U)"),
  answer("exp(-2 * U)"),
  answer("log(U) * 2"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q6}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q6"]],
  answer("0.5, the mean 1/rate, by the law of large numbers", correct = TRUE),
  answer("2, the rate"),
  answer("0.25, the variance"),
  answer("1, because the exponential is memoryless"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## Sampling distribution of the mean

```{r clt-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=10}
set.seed(2027)
xbar <- replicate(5000, mean(sample(len, 30, replace = TRUE)))
c(mean = mean(xbar), sd = sd(xbar), theory = sigma / sqrt(30))
mean(xbar > 700)
1 - pnorm(700, mu, sigma / sqrt(30))
```

## Submit

Type your name, download the text file, and upload it. Submit the questions first so the file contains your answers. If nothing downloads, the same `.txt` is in this folder: select it in the Files pane and choose Export.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts,
      open = lab_meta$open
    )
    # The viewer in Posit Cloud often blocks the browser download.
    file.copy(
      file,
      lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
      overwrite = TRUE
    )
  }
)
```
